Today (November 26, New Calendar) the Church remembers our Venerable Father Alypius the Stylite.

He was from Adrianopolis in Bithynia and took up the ascetical life at a young age. After many spiritual struggles he went to live on a pillar, where he dwelt for fifty-three years. Crowds came to seek his intercession and counsel, and in time a women’s monastery was founded near the pillar.

He owned nothing, and once threw his only tunic down to a poor man in need. After a stroke paralyzed half his body, he lived on the pillar for another fourteen years, giving up his soul to God at the age of ninety-nine.

Venerable Father Alypius, pray to God for us.
